## Appendix E Stability

### E.1 Notation

To assist the demonstration of the proof of our stability results, we define the following quantities. Let

$$ \overline{M}^{2}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime}):=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\|\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{w})-\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{w}^{\prime})\|_{2}^{2}\quad\text{and}\quad\overline{G}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime}):=\|\nabla F(\mathbf{w})-\nabla F(\mathbf{w}^{\prime})\|_{2}^{2}. $$

One can see that $\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})=\frac{\overline{M}^{2}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})}{\overline{G}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})}$ . We also define

$$ \overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}=\inf_{\mathbf{w}\neq\mathbf{w}^{\prime}}\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime}). $$

### E.2 Proof of Theorem 12 and Corollary 3

We first recall the problem setting. Suppose that there are two sample sets $\mathcal{S}$ and $\mathcal{S}^{(I)}$ which differs at one data point located at a random position $I$ , which is uniformly distributed in $[n]$ . We run the same (projected) parallel mini-batch SGD on both data sets, and after the $k$ -th parallel iteration, we obtain $\mathbf{w}_{kB}$ and $\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}$ , respectively. After a total number of $T$ gradient updates, i.e., $T/B$ parallel iterations, we obtain $\mathbf{w}_{T}$ and $\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{T}$ . Let $s_{t}$ , $t=0,1,\ldots,T-1$ be the sequence of indices of samples used by the algorithm. In our setting, $s_{t}$ are i.i.d. uniformly distributed in $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ . Let $\mathbf{z}_{s_{t}}\in\mathcal{S}$ and $\widetilde{\mathbf{z}}_{s_{t}}\in\mathcal{S}^{(I)}$ , $t=0,\ldots,T-1$ be the data point used in the algorithms running on the two data sets, respectively. Then, we know that with probability $1-\frac{1}{n}$ , $\mathbf{z}_{s_{t}}=\widetilde{\mathbf{z}}_{s_{t}}$ , and with probability $\frac{1}{n}$ , $\mathbf{z}_{s_{t}}\neq\widetilde{\mathbf{z}}_{s_{t}}$ . We simplify the notations of the risk function associated with $\mathbf{z}_{s_{t}}$ and $\widetilde{\mathbf{z}}_{s_{t}}$ by $f_{s_{t}}(\mathbf{w}):=f(\mathbf{w};\mathbf{z}_{s_{t}})$ , and $\widetilde{f}_{s_{t}}(\mathbf{w}):=f(\mathbf{w};\widetilde{\mathbf{z}}_{s_{t}})$ , respectively.

We now prove Theorem 12. Throughout this proof, we only consider the case where $B>1$ and omit the indicator function $\mathds{1}_{B>1}$ . We condition on the data sets and the event that the choice of $\gamma$ is “good”, as shown in (9). Specifically, we condition on the samples $\mathcal{S}$ and $\mathcal{S}^{\prime}$ , and the event $\Gamma$ :

$$ \Gamma=\left\{\gamma\leq\frac{2}{\beta(1+\frac{1}{n-1}+\frac{B-1}{\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}})}\right\}=\left\{\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}\geq\frac{B-1}{\frac{2}{\gamma\beta}-1-\frac{1}{n-1}}\right\}. $$

Our goal is to bound $\left|\epsilon_{\text{stab}}(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}^{\prime})\right|$ . Since we assume that $f(\mathbf{w};\mathbf{z})$ is $L$ -Lipschitz on $\mathcal{W}$ , we have

$$ \left|\epsilon_{\text{stab}}(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}^{\prime})\right|\leq L\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid\Gamma}\left[\|A(\mathcal{S}^{(I)})-A(\mathcal{S})\|_{2}\right]=L\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid\Gamma}\left[\|\mathbf{w}_{T}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{T}\|_{2}\right], $$

and thus it suffices to bound $\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid\Gamma}\left[\|\mathbf{w}_{T}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{T}\|_{2}\right]$ .

Consider the samples used in the $(k+1)$ -th parallel iteration in the two algorithm instances, i.e., $\{\mathbf{z}_{s_{t}}\}_{t=kB}^{(k+1)B-1}$ , and $\{\widetilde{\mathbf{z}}_{s_{t}}\}_{t=kB}^{(k+1)B-1}$ . Let $H_{k+1}$ be the number of instances that the two data points with the same index being different in these two sample sets (i.e., $s_{t}=I$ ). According to our sampling scheme, $H_{k+1}\sim\text{bin}(B,\frac{1}{n})$ . We condition on the event that $H_{k+1}=h$ . Without loss of generality, we assume that $\mathbf{z}_{s_{t}}=\widetilde{\mathbf{z}}_{s_{t}}$ for all $t=kB,\ldots,(k+1)B-h-1$ , and $\mathbf{z}_{s_{t}}\neq\widetilde{\mathbf{z}}_{s_{t}}$ for all $t=(k+1)B-h,\ldots,(k+1)B-1$ . Consider the first $B-h$ terms. For the unconstrained optimization, we have

$$ \|\mathbf{w}_{(k+1)B-h}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{(k+1)B-h}\|_{2}^{2}=\|(\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\gamma\sum_{t=kB}^{(k+1)B-h-1}\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB}))-(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}-\gamma\sum_{t=kB}^{(k+1)B-h-1}\nabla\widetilde{f}_{s_{t}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}))\|_{2}^{2}. $$

For the algorithm with projection, the $B$ gradient update steps are the same as the unconstrained algorithm, and projection step is conducted once all the gradient updates are finished. Therefore, (27) also holds for projected algorithm.

Since $f_{s_{t}}(\mathbf{w})=\widetilde{f}_{s_{t}}(\mathbf{w})$ for all $t=kB,\ldots,(k+1)B-h-1$ , we further have

$$ \displaystyle\|\mathbf{w}_{(k+1)B-h}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{(k+1)B-h}\|_{2}^{2} \displaystyle= \displaystyle\|\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}\|_{2}^{2}-2\langle\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB},\gamma\sum_{t=kB}^{(k+1)B-h-1}\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})\rangle \displaystyle+\gamma^{2}\|\sum_{t=kB}^{(k+1)B-h-1}\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})\|_{2}^{2} \displaystyle= \displaystyle\|\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}\|_{2}^{2}-2\langle\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB},\gamma\sum_{t=kB}^{(k+1)B-h-1}\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})\rangle \displaystyle+\gamma^{2}\sum_{t=kB}^{(k+1)B-h-1}\|\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})\|_{2}^{2} \displaystyle+2\gamma^{2}\sum_{i=kB}^{(k+1)B-h-1}\sum_{j=i+1}^{(k+1)B-h-1}\langle\nabla f_{s_{i}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{i}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}),\nabla f_{s_{j}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{j}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})\rangle. $$

We denote the sequence of indices selected by the mini-batch SGD algorithm up to the $t$ -th sampled data point as $A_{t}$ , i.e., $A_{t}=\{s_{0},\ldots,s_{t-1}\}$ . In the following steps, we condition on $A_{kB}$ and the event that $H_{k+1}=h$ , and take expectation over the randomness of the SGD algorithm in the $(k+1)$ -th parallel iteration and the random choice of $I$ .

We consider each term in (28). For the term $\|\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})\|_{2}^{2}$ , conditioned on the event that $\mathbf{z}_{s_{t}}=\widetilde{\mathbf{z}}_{s_{t}}$ , we know that $s_{t}$ is uniformly distributed in $[n]\setminus\{I\}$ . Since $I$ is uniformly distributed in $[n]$ , we know that the marginal distribution of $s_{t}$ is uniform in $[n]$ . We have

$$ \mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid H_{k+1},A_{kB},\Gamma}[\|\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})\|_{2}^{2}]=\overline{M}^{2}(\mathbf{w}_{kB},\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}). $$

Then we find the conditional expectation of $\langle\nabla f_{s_{i}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{i}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}),\nabla f_{s_{j}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{j}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})\rangle$ . We have the following lemma.

#### Lemma 3.

For any $i,j$ such that $kB\leq i,j\leq(k+1)B-h-1$ and $i\neq j$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid H_{k+1},A_{kB},\Gamma}[\langle\nabla f_{s_{i}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{i}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}),\nabla f_{s_{j}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{j}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})\rangle] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{1}{(n-1)^{2}}\overline{M}^{2}(\mathbf{w}_{kB},\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})+\frac{n(n-2)}{(n-1)^{2}}\overline{G}(\mathbf{w}_{kB},\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}). $$

We prove Lemma 3 in Appendix E.4. According to this lemma, we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid H_{k+1},A_{kB},\Gamma}[\|\mathbf{w}_{(k+1)B-h}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{(k+1)B-h}\|_{2}^{2}] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\|\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}\|_{2}^{2}-2\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid H_{k+1},A_{kB},\Gamma}[\langle\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB},\gamma\sum_{t=kB}^{(k+1)B-h-1}\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})\rangle] \displaystyle+\gamma^{2}(B-h)\overline{M}^{2}(\mathbf{w}_{kB},\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}) \displaystyle+\gamma^{2}(B-h)(B-h-1)\left[\frac{1}{(n-1)^{2}}\overline{M}^{2}(\mathbf{w}_{kB},\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})+\frac{n(n-2)}{(n-1)^{2}}\overline{G}(\mathbf{w}_{kB},\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})\right] \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\|\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}\|_{2}^{2}-2\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid H_{k+1},A_{kB},\Gamma}[\langle\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB},\gamma\sum_{t=kB}^{(k+1)B-h-1}\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})\rangle] \displaystyle+\gamma^{2}(B-h)\overline{M}^{2}(\mathbf{w}_{kB},\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})+\gamma^{2}(B-h)\left[\frac{1}{n-1}\overline{M}^{2}(\mathbf{w}_{kB},\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})+(B-1)\frac{\overline{M}^{2}(\mathbf{w}_{kB},\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})}{\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB},\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})}\right] \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\|\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}\|_{2}^{2}-2\gamma\sum_{t=kB}^{(k+1)B-h-1}\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid H_{k+1},A_{kB},\Gamma}[\langle\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB},\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})\rangle] \displaystyle+\gamma^{2}(B-h)(1+\frac{1}{n-1}+\frac{B-1}{\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}})\overline{M}^{2}(\mathbf{w}_{kB},\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}). $$

By the co-coercive property of convex and smooth functions, we know that

$$ \langle\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB},\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})\rangle\geq\frac{1}{\beta}\|\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})\|_{2}^{2}. $$

Then, we obtain

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid H_{k+1},A_{kB},\Gamma} \displaystyle[\|\mathbf{w}_{(k+1)B-h}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{(k+1)B-h}\|_{2}^{2}]\leq\|\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}\|_{2}^{2} \displaystyle-(2\frac{\gamma}{\beta}-\gamma^{2}(1+\frac{1}{n-1}+\frac{B-1}{\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}}))(B-h)\overline{M}^{2}(\mathbf{w}_{kB},\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}). $$

Since we condition on good choice of $\gamma$ in (25), we have

$$ \mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid H_{k+1},A_{kB},\Gamma}[\|\mathbf{w}_{(k+1)B-h}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{(k+1)B-h}\|_{2}^{2}]\leq\|\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}\|_{2}^{2}. $$

Then by Jensen’s inequality, we have

$$ \mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid H_{k+1},A_{kB},\Gamma}[\|\mathbf{w}_{(k+1)B-h}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{(k+1)B-h}\|_{2}]\leq\|\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}\|_{2}. $$

For the last $h$ terms, since the loss functions are all $L$ -Lipschitz, we obtain

$$ \|\mathbf{w}_{(k+1)B}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{(k+1)B}\|_{2}\leq\|\mathbf{w}_{(k+1)B-h}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{(k+1)B-h}\|_{2}+2\gamma Lh. $$

Then, combining with equation (32), we have

$$ \mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid H_{k+1},A_{kB},\Gamma}[\|\mathbf{w}_{(k+1)B}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{(k+1)B}\|_{2}]\leq\|\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}\|_{2}+2\gamma Lh. $$

Taking expectation over $H_{k+1}$ yields

$$ \mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid A_{kB},\Gamma}[\|\mathbf{w}_{(k+1)B}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{(k+1)B}\|_{2}]\leq\|\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}\|_{2}+2\gamma L\frac{B}{n}. $$

Then we take expectation over the randomness of the first $k$ parallel iterations and obtain

$$ \mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid\Gamma}[\|\mathbf{w}_{(k+1)B}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{(k+1)B}\|_{2}]\leq\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid\Gamma}[\|\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}\|_{2}]+2\gamma L\frac{B}{n}. $$

Summing up (35) for $k=0,1,\ldots,\frac{T}{B}-1$ and taking expectation over the data sets, we have

$$ \mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid\Gamma}[\|\mathbf{w}_{T}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{T}\|_{2}]\leq 2\gamma L\frac{T}{n}. $$

Combining equations (26) and (36), we complete the proof of Theorem 12, i.e., when $\Gamma$ happens,

$$ \left|\epsilon_{\text{stab}}(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}^{\prime})\right|\leq L\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid\Gamma}\left[\|\mathbf{w}_{T}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{T}\|_{2}\right]\leq 2\gamma L^{2}\frac{T}{n}. $$

To prove Corollary 3, we notice the fact that when $\Gamma$ does not happen, we simply have

$$ \left|\epsilon_{\text{stab}}(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}^{\prime})\right|\leq L\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid\bar{\Gamma}}[\|\mathbf{w}_{T}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{T}\|_{2}]\leq 2\gamma L^{2}T. $$

According to (10), $\eta=\mathbb{P}\{\bar{\Gamma}\}$ . Then, according to (37) and (38), we get

$$ \displaystyle\epsilon_{\text{gen}} \displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}^{\prime}\mid\Gamma}\left[\left|\epsilon_{\text{stab}}(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}^{\prime})\right|\right]\mathbb{P}\{\Gamma\}+\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}^{\prime}\mid\bar{\Gamma}}\left[\left|\epsilon_{\text{stab}}(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}^{\prime})\right|\right]\mathbb{P}\{\bar{\Gamma}\} \displaystyle\leq 2\gamma L^{2}\frac{T}{n}(1-\eta)+2\gamma L^{2}T\eta, $$

which completes the proof.

### E.3 Proof of Theorem 13 and Corollary 4

The proof of Theorem 13 follows an argument similar to the proof of Theorem 12. We define the event $\Gamma$ that the step size is “good” in the following way, as shown in (11) (slightly different from the convex risk functions):

$$ \Gamma=\left\{\gamma\leq\frac{2}{(\beta+\lambda)(1+\frac{1}{n-1}+\frac{B-1}{\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}})}\right\}=\left\{\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}\geq\frac{B-1}{\frac{2}{\gamma(\beta+\lambda)}-1-\frac{1}{n-1}}\right\}. $$

To prove Theorem 13, our goal is still to bound $\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid\Gamma}\left[\|\mathbf{w}_{T}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{T}\|_{2}\right]$ . Since the result in (30) still holds for strongly convex functions, we can obtain

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid H_{k+1},A_{kB},\Gamma}[\|\mathbf{w}_{(k+1)B-h}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{(k+1)B-h}\|_{2}^{2}] \displaystyle\leq \displaystyle\|\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}\|_{2}^{2}-2\gamma\sum_{t=kB}^{(k+1)B-h-1}\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid H_{k+1},A_{kB},\Gamma}[\langle\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB},\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})\rangle] \displaystyle+\gamma^{2}(B-h)(1+\frac{1}{n-1}+\frac{B-1}{\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}})\overline{M}^{2}(\mathbf{w}_{kB},\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}), $$

where $H_{k+1}$ is defined in the same way as in the proof of Theorem 12. For strongly convex functions, we have the following co-coercive property:

$$ \langle\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB},\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})\rangle\geq\frac{\beta\lambda}{\beta+\lambda}\|\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}\|_{2}^{2}+\frac{1}{\beta+\lambda}\|\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{t}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})\|_{2}^{2}, $$

which gives us

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid H_{k+1},A_{kB},\Gamma} \displaystyle[\|\mathbf{w}_{(k+1)B-h}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{(k+1)B-h}\|_{2}^{2}]\leq\left(1-2\gamma(B-h)\frac{\beta\lambda}{\beta+\lambda}\right)\|\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}\|_{2}^{2} \displaystyle-\gamma(B-h)\left[\frac{2}{\beta+\lambda}-\gamma(1+\frac{1}{n-1}+\frac{B-1}{\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}})\right]\overline{M}^{2}(\mathbf{w}_{kB},\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}). $$

Since we only consider the regime where $B\leq\frac{1}{2\gamma\lambda}$ , one can check that $1-2\gamma(B-h)\frac{\beta\lambda}{\beta+\lambda}>0$ for any $h=0,\ldots,B$ . Conditioned on the data sets and the good choice of $\gamma$ , we have

$$ \mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid H_{k+1},A_{kB},\Gamma}[\|\mathbf{w}_{(k+1)B-h}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{(k+1)B-h}\|_{2}^{2}]\leq\left(1-2\gamma B\frac{\beta\lambda}{\beta+\lambda}\right)\|\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}\|_{2}^{2}. $$

With Jensen’s inequality and the fact that $\sqrt{1-x}\leq 1-\frac{x}{2}$ for any $x\in[0,1]$ , we have

$$ \mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid H_{k+1},A_{kB},\Gamma}[\|\mathbf{w}_{(k+1)B-h}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{(k+1)B-h}\|_{2}]\leq\left(1-\gamma B\frac{\beta\lambda}{\beta+\lambda}\right)\|\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}\|_{2}. $$

For the last $h$ terms, we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid H_{k+1},A_{kB},\Gamma}[\|\mathbf{w}_{(k+1)B}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{(k+1)B}\|_{2}]\leq\|\mathbf{w}_{(k+1)B-h}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{(k+1)B-h}\|_{2}+2\gamma Lh. $$

Combined with equation (43), we obtain

$$ \mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid H_{k+1},A_{kB},\Gamma}[\|\mathbf{w}_{(k+1)B}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{(k+1)B}\|_{2}]\leq\left(1-\gamma B\frac{\beta\lambda}{\beta+\lambda}\right)\|\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}\|_{2}+2\gamma Lh, $$

and by taking expectation over $h$ we have

$$ \mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid A_{kB},\Gamma}[\|\mathbf{w}_{(k+1)B}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{(k+1)B}\|_{2}]\leq\left(1-\gamma B\frac{\beta\lambda}{\beta+\lambda}\right)\|\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}\|_{2}+2\gamma L\frac{B}{n}. $$

Taking expectation over $A_{kB}$ yields

$$ \mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid\Gamma}[\|\mathbf{w}_{(k+1)B}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{(k+1)B}\|_{2}]\leq\left(1-\gamma B\frac{\beta\lambda}{\beta+\lambda}\right)\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid\Gamma}[\|\mathbf{w}_{kB}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}\|_{2}]+2\gamma L\frac{B}{n}. $$

Iterating equation (45) yields

$$ \mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid\Gamma}[\|\mathbf{w}_{T}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{T}\|_{2}]\leq\frac{4L}{\lambda n}. $$

Combining equations (26) and (46), we prove Theorem 13, i.e., when $\Gamma$ happens,

$$ \left|\epsilon_{\text{stab}}(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}^{\prime})\right|\leq L\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid\Gamma}\left[\|\mathbf{w}_{T}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{T}\|_{2}\right]\leq\frac{4L^{2}}{\lambda n}. $$

To prove Corollary 4, we notice the fact that, when $\Gamma$ does not occur, we simply have

$$ \left|\epsilon_{\text{stab}}(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}^{\prime})\right|\leq L\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid\bar{\Gamma}}[\|\mathbf{w}_{T}-\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{T}\|_{2}]\leq 2\gamma L^{2}T. $$

According to (12), $\eta=\mathbb{P}\{\bar{\Gamma}\}$ . Then, according to (47) and (48), we get

$$ \displaystyle\epsilon_{\text{gen}} \displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}^{\prime}\mid\Gamma}\left[\left|\epsilon_{\text{stab}}(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}^{\prime})\right|\right]\mathbb{P}\{\Gamma\}+\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}^{\prime}\mid\bar{\Gamma}}\left[\left|\epsilon_{\text{stab}}(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{S}^{\prime})\right|\right]\mathbb{P}\{\bar{\Gamma}\} \displaystyle\leq\frac{4L^{2}}{\lambda n}(1-\eta)+2\gamma L^{2}T\eta, $$

which completes the proof.

### E.4 Proof of Lemma 3

One can interpret $\overline{M}^{2}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})$ and $\overline{G}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})$ as follows. Let $\mathcal{P}_{1}$ be a distribution on $[n]\times[n]$ with PMF

$$ p_{1}(u,v)=\frac{1}{n}\mathds{1}_{u=v}, $$

and $\mathcal{P}_{2}$ be the uniform distribution on $[n]\times[n]$ , i.e.,

$$ p_{2}(u,v)=\frac{1}{n^{2}} $$

for all $(u,v)\in[n]\times[n]$ . Then, we know that

$$ \overline{M}^{2}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})=\mathbb{E}_{(i,j)\sim\mathcal{P}_{1}}[\langle\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{w})-\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{w}^{\prime}),\nabla f_{j}(\mathbf{w})-\nabla f_{j}(\mathbf{w}^{\prime})\rangle], $$

and

$$ \overline{G}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})=\mathbb{E}_{(i,j)\sim\mathcal{P}_{2}}[\langle\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{w})-\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{w}^{\prime}),\nabla f_{j}(\mathbf{w})-\nabla f_{j}(\mathbf{w}^{\prime})\rangle]. $$

Then we find the joint distribution $\mathcal{P}_{3}$ of $(s_{i},s_{j})$ where $kB\leq i,j\leq(k+1)B-h-1$ and $i\neq j$ . Since $\mathbf{z}_{s_{t}}=\widetilde{\mathbf{z}}_{s_{t}}$ , we know that $s_{t}\neq I$ for all $t=kB,\ldots,(k+1)B-h-1$ . Then conditioned on $I$ , $(s_{i},s_{j})$ is uniformly distributed in $([n]\setminus\{I\})\times([n]\setminus\{I\})$ . For any $u\in[n]$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle p_{3}(u,u) \displaystyle=\mathbb{P}\{s_{i}=u,s_{j}=u\}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{\ell=1}^{n}\mathbb{P}\{s_{i}=u,s_{j}=u\mid I=\ell\} \displaystyle=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{\ell=u}\mathbb{P}\{s_{i}=u,s_{j}=u\mid I=\ell\}=\frac{1}{n(n-1)}. $$

For any $(u,v)\in[n]\times[n]$ such that $u\neq v$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle p_{3}(u,v) \displaystyle=\mathbb{P}\{s_{i}=u,s_{j}=v\}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{\ell=1}^{n}\mathbb{P}\{s_{i}=u,s_{j}=v\mid I=\ell\} \displaystyle=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{\ell\neq u,v}\mathbb{P}\{s_{i}=u,s_{j}=v\mid I=\ell\} \displaystyle=\frac{n-2}{n(n-1)^{2}}. $$

Then, we know that

$$ p_{3}(u,v)=\frac{1}{(n-1)^{2}}p_{1}(u,v)+\frac{n(n-2)}{(n-1)^{2}}p_{2}(u,v). $$

Therefore, for any $i,j$ such that $kB\leq i,j\leq(k+1)B-h-1$ and $i\neq j$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{I,A\mid H_{k+1},A_{kB},\Gamma}[\langle\nabla f_{s_{i}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{i}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}),\nabla f_{s_{j}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{j}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})\rangle] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{(s_{i},s_{j})\sim\mathcal{P}_{3}}[\langle\nabla f_{s_{i}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{i}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}),\nabla f_{s_{j}}(\mathbf{w}_{kB})-\nabla f_{s_{j}}(\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})\rangle] \displaystyle= \displaystyle\frac{1}{(n-1)^{2}}\overline{M}^{2}(\mathbf{w}_{kB},\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB})+\frac{n(n-2)}{(n-1)^{2}}\overline{G}(\mathbf{w}_{kB},\widetilde{\mathbf{w}}_{kB}). $$

### E.5 Examples of Differential Gradient Diversity and Diversity-inducing Mechanisms

#### Generalized Linear Functions

We can show that for generalized linear functions, the lower bound in Theorem 1 still holds, i.e., , for any $\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{W}$ , $\mathbf{w}\neq\mathbf{w}^{\prime}$ , we have

$$ \overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})\geq\frac{\min_{i=1,\ldots,n}\|\mathbf{x}_{i}\|_{2}^{2}}{\sigma_{\max}^{2}(\mathbf{X})}. $$

To see this, one can simply replace $\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{w})$ with $\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{w})-\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{w}^{\prime})$ in Appendix A.1, and define $a_{i}=\ell_{i}^{\prime}(\mathbf{x}_{i}^{\rm T}\mathbf{w})-\ell_{i}^{\prime}(\mathbf{x}_{i}^{\rm T}\mathbf{w}^{\prime})$ . The same arguments in Appendix A.1 still go through. Consequently, for i.i.d. $\sigma$ -sub-Gaussian features, we have $\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})\geq c_{1}d$ $\forall~\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{W}$ with probability at least $1-c_{2}ne^{-c_{3}d}$ ; and for Rademacher entries, we have $\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})\geq c_{4}d$ $\forall~\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{W}$ with probability greater than $1-c_{5}e^{-c_{6}n}$ .

#### Sparse Conflicts

The result in Theorem 2 still holds for $\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})$ , i.e., for all $\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime}\in\mathcal{W}$ , $\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})\geq n/(\rho+1)$ , where $\rho$ is the maximum degree of all the vertices in the conflict graph $G$ . To see this, one should notice that the support of $\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{w})$ only depends on the data point, instead of the model parameter, and thus, in general, $\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{w})$ and $\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{w})-\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{w}^{\prime})$ have the same support. Then, one can simply replace $\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{w})$ with $\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{w})-\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{w}^{\prime})$ in Appendix A.3 and the same arguments still go through.

#### Dropout

When we analyze the stability of mini-batch SGD, we apply the same algorithm to two different samples $\mathcal{S}$ and $\mathcal{S}^{(I)}$ that only differ at one data point. Since the algorithm is the same, the random dropout matrices $\mathbf{D}_{1},\ldots,\mathbf{D}_{n}$ are also the same in the two instances. Therefore, one can replace $\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{w})$ with $\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{w})-\nabla f_{i}(\mathbf{w}^{\prime})$ , and the same arguments still work. Then, we know that when $\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})\leq n$ , we have $\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}^{\sf{drop}}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})\geq\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})$ , and when $\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})>n$ , we have $\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}^{\sf{drop}}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})>n$ .

#### Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics

For SGLD, we can make similar arguments as in dropout, since the additive noise vectors $\xi_{1},\ldots,\xi_{n}$ are the same for the two instances. One can then show that when $\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})\leq n$ , we have $\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}^{\sf{sgld}}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})\geq\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})$ , and when $\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})>n$ , we have $\overline{B}_{\mathcal{S}}^{\sf{sgld}}(\mathbf{w},\mathbf{w}^{\prime})>n$ .
